data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个通过RPG游戏学习证明理论的工具（algae）的用户体验和技术反馈

不同观点：

• **正面体验派**：nanolith通关了游戏并认为与《The Little Prover》类似；Vedor称赞新手友好且移动端可玩；marktani通过逆向工程成功掌握了规则

• **改进建议派**：bartleeanderson建议战斗前先提供教程；shiandow批评wip替换qed的设计过于繁琐，认为缩进已经表明了结构

• **标题误解派**：adamddev1和pjmlp误以为是RPG编程语言（IBM RPG），建议标题中加"an"来明确是角色扮演游戏

• **技术问题派**：wizzwizz4报告严重bug，某些sphinx无法加载导致游戏卡住无法进度

补充讨论：开发者geckones承认AI生成的证明质量不理想，难度递进缺失，需要手动修复每个证明。项目目标是提供学习证明理论的游乐场，但目前在教程设计和稳定性上仍需改进。

data.title: The Private Capture of Public Genius
data.author: martialg
data.article_summary:
1956年，作为世界最大私营公司的AT&T被迫签署反垄断和解协议，无偿开放全部7,820项未到期专利给美国企业，并限制其只能经营电信业务。尽管AT&T旗下的贝尔实验室凭借公共补贴创造了晶体管、信息论等重大发明，但监管者认为其垄断地位危险。

这些专利中69%与电信无关，涉及半导体、化学等多个领域。专利开放后数年内产生约60亿美元后续价值，其中35亿来自初创公司。这直接催生了从仙童半导体到英特尔的创新链条，奠定了硅谷发展基础。

英特尔联合创始人戈登·摩尔后来评价：这是美国商业半导体产业起步的最重要事件之一。文章探讨了公共资助的科研成果如何通过反垄断措施释放，引发创新爆发。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点**：AI训练数据使用的合法性、补偿机制及公共资源的私有化问题

**不同观点**：

• **全球补偿派**（marcus_holmes）：训练数据来自全世界，应通过联合国建立全球性补偿机制，优先用于扶贫而非仅补偿美国人

• **质疑价值派**（PaulDavisThe1st, typ）：认为文章夸大了LLM在前沿科学中的作用；公共知识应自由使用，不应特殊征税，大部分社交媒体内容价值有限

• **历史必然派**（schnitzelstoat）：类比棉花轧花机专利案，认为经济重要性会让法律对侵权睁一只眼闭一只眼，"如果我们不做，中国就会做"

• **版权澄清派**（pgisapedo）：强调生成受版权保护内容本身不违法，只有商业销售才构成侵权

• **公共资源派**（willturman）：借鉴水资源公共信托案例，主张建立可选加入的公共知识共享库，而非事后索赔

• **价值交换派**（stale2002）：认为开源模型扩散使价值提取不切实际，且AI实验室创造的公共价值可能已超过其"窃取"的价值

**补充讨论**：
• w10-1指出雇主强制员工自动化自身工作的剥削性更直接
• zombot和abalashov将此定性为"人类历史最大抢劫"和伦理冒犯
• 多人关注开源模型对权力结构的影响

The Private Capture of Public Genius
Essay I of Upstream of Everything
Jul 02, 2026

On January 24, 1956, the American Telephone and Telegraph Company was the largest private company in the world.
Its revenues amounted to almost 2% of the U.S. gross domestic product. It employed 746,000 people. It owned Bell Labs, the fabled research division that had already produced the transistor, the solar cell, information theory, and radio astronomy, while also actively laying the first transatlantic telephone cable. In the following decades, it would add UNIX, modern cellular telephony, the CCD image sensor, the first active communications satellite, and a long list of other scientific milestones. This singular stretch of intellectual output paved the way for Bell scientists to eventually collect five Turing Awards and ten Nobel Prizes.
By many metrics, life as a regulated monopoly was very good for AT&T.
Yet by the end of the day AT&T had signed away exclusive rights to every single one of its 7,820 unexpired patents, royalty-free, to any American firm that asked. AT&T would also license any future patents it filed at “reasonable rates.” A bleeding-edge, intellectual property treasure hoard was suddenly and irrevocably opened to the free market.
Antitrust officials initially sold the settlement as a triumph. The Justice Department called it a major victory, with one DOJ lawyer hailing it as “miraculous.” Despite AT&T already existing for decades as a regulated monopoly, with its returns constrained to a relatively conservative (by today’s standards) ~7% per annum, government regulators had pursued and established a landmark set of additional restrictions to curtail AT&T’s monopoly power.
Soon, however, public sentiment started to shift.
Business Week
called the decree “hardly more than a slap on the wrist.” A House congressional subcommittee would later deem it “a blot on the enforcement history of antitrust laws” for its perceived lenience on AT&T’s exclusive supply chains and vertical integration. Both the ratepayers, who subsidized AT&T’s vast research budget through its rate contracts, and many in the federal government believed this unprecedented economic concentration to still be far too dangerous for the Republic to continue unabated.
The now-infamous 1956 patent decree was just one half of a settlement negotiated over seven years between AT&T and the federal government. AT&T wanted to continue manufacturing telephone equipment through its subsidiary Western Electric, but regulators believed the vertical integration was foreclosing competition within the industry. The federal government itself was so conflicted about this issue that Secretary of Defense under President Eisenhower, Charles Wilson, pleaded with litigators that severing AT&T from Western Electric was “contrary to the vital interests of our nation.”
The second half of the settlement barred Bell from pursuing any business other than telecommunications.
A later analysis of the historical record revealed that 69% of Bell’s patents had little to do with telecom. Rather, they ranged from chemistry to semiconductors to metalworking, lighting, optics, and more.
The two halves of the settlement combined to ensure that this rich intellectual corpus, roughly 1.3% of all unexpired American patents at the time, became freely available essentially overnight
and
had a guarantee from Uncle Sam that the big, bad Bell Labs legal wolf would not come knocking.
Within just a few years, these released patents would generate almost $6B in follow-on patent value outside of the telecom industry. About $3.5B of that value came from patents filed by young, startup companies. One famous branch of that startup explosion ran through Shockley Semiconductor, then Fairchild Semiconductor, and eventually into the storied company known as Intel.
Intel’s co-founder, Gordon Moore (of Moore’s Law fame), would later describe this consent-decree-driven innovation cascade as:
“One of the most important developments for the commercial semiconductor industry. [It] allowed the merchant semiconductor industry to really get started in the United States. There is a direct connection between the liberal licensing policies of Bell Labs and people such as Gordon Teal leaving Bell Labs to start Texas Instruments and William Shockley doing the same thing to start Shockley Semiconductor in Palo Alto.
This started the growth of Silicon Valley.”
Sediment
A generation of brilliant, publicly subsidized scientists built one of the most impactful clusters of technical genius the world has ever seen. Bell generated patents, invented products, and became the undisputed epicenter of American frontier science for decades. But how?

data.title: Kani: A Model Checker for Rust
data.author: Jimmc414
data.article_summary: Kani是一个面向Rust语言的开源模型检查器。虽然Rust的所有权系统能防止内存错误，但不安全操作的正确性、功能正确性和运行时panic仍需验证。Kani将Rust中级中间表示（MIR）编译到CBMC验证引擎，自动检查安全属性。它提供包括函数契约、循环契约和量词的规范语言，将验证从有界扩展到无界。在工业项目案例研究中，Kani发现了6个未知bug，并已在生产CI中大规模应用——在Rust标准库验证活动中，每次代码变更会验证超过16,000个测试用例。该研究已被ASE 2026工业展示track接收。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kani Rust Verifier工具的功能、应用和相关资源

不同观点：

• **实用性认可派**：ZeroCool2u认为教程很有帮助，并将Kani与Python的hypothesis-auto工具进行类比，认为在简单应用场景下两者有相似之处

• **功能探索派**：ramon156对工具的能力边界表示疑问，询问是否仅限于边界检查、溢出和除零错误检测，同时对模型检查器这一技术表示兴趣，认为它在测试框架中会很强大

• **学术背景派**：ototot分享了工具的学术论文（2022年ACM论文），为讨论提供理论基础

• **替代方案派**：rando1234推荐了另一个Rust模型检查工具，该工具更专注于检测并发bug，暗示不同工具有不同的专长领域

补充讨论：dang提供了2022年3月的历史讨论链接，说明这个工具已经受到社区关注一段时间。整体讨论氛围是信息分享和技术探讨，没有明显的争议点，更多是对工具功能范围和应用场景的好奇与探索。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Rust's ownership type system prevents memory errors in safe code, but certain desirable properties remain orthogonal to compilation: the soundness of unsafe operations (e.g., raw pointer dereferences), functional correctness, and absence of runtime panics. We present Kani, an open-source model checker for Rust that pushes bounded model checking beyond bug-finding to provide correctness guarantees for these properties. Kani compiles proof harnesses from Rust's Mid-level Intermediate Representation (MIR) into CBMC's bit-precise verification engine, automatically checking a comprehensive set of safety properties with no user annotation. To extend verification from bounded to unbounded, Kani provides a specification language comprising function contracts, loop contracts, quantifiers, and function stubbing. We demonstrate feasibility through case studies on industrial Rust projects, where contracts upgraded verification from panic-freedom to functional correctness, uncovering six previously unknown bugs. Kani operates at scale in production CI, with over 16,000 harnesses verified per code change in the Rust standard library verification campaign.

data.title: OfficeCLI: Office suite for AI agents to read and edit Microsoft Office files
data.author: maxloh
data.article_summary:
OfficeCLI是首个专为AI代理设计的开源Office套件，通过单一二进制文件让AI完全控制Word、Excel和PowerPoint，无需安装Office或任何依赖。

核心特性包括：
- 内置HTML渲染引擎，可将文档渲染为HTML或PNG，实现"渲染→查看→修复"闭环
- 一行代码即可集成到AI代理中
- 支持创建、读取、分析和修改文档的所有操作
- 提供实时预览功能（watch命令）
- 输出结构化JSON数据

最大优势是极大简化了文档操作——原本需要50行Python代码和多个库才能完成的任务，现在只需一条命令即可实现。跨平台支持macOS、Linux和Windows，适合开发者和AI代理使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对AI代理操作Office文档的工具开发，涉及技术路线选择、实用性评估和企业应用需求

不同观点：

• **技术标准派**：强调ECMA 376标准合规性对无头生成和处理的重要性，认为这是专业实现的基础（rcarmo、jbgt）

• **实用质疑派**：质疑专用工具的必要性 - 认为直接用Python/Claude Code可能在提示遵循度、视觉效果和token消耗方面更优；或认为LaTeX等替代方案更适合（allan_s、beepbooptheory）

• **企业问责派**：指出真正难点不在生成而在验证 - 企业文档需要引用、数据、格式、语义的验证机制，否则无法实际应用（StahlGuo）

• **替代方案派**：建议非交互场景用HTML转PDF方案，体验更好（pietz）

• **趋同观察派**：多位开发者注意到类似想法同时涌现，认为这是有趣的市场信号，同时也在开发类似工具（jbgt、topaztee）

补充讨论：评论中出现商标使用争议（neilv批评"Office"称呼不当）、功能细节咨询（Excel公式/宏处理、LibreOffice支持）以及对token优化价值的认可。整体反映出AI文档自动化工具正处于探索期，实现路径和应用价值仍存在分歧。

48807225.article_summary:
OfficeCLI是首个专为AI代理设计的开源Office套件，通过单一二进制文件让AI完全控制Word、Excel和PowerPoint，无需安装Office或任何依赖。

核心特性包括：
- 内置HTML渲染引擎，可将文档渲染为HTML或PNG，实现"渲染→查看→修复"闭环
- 一行代码即可集成到AI代理中
- 支持创建、读取、分析和修改文档的所有操作
- 提供实时预览功能（watch命令）
- 输出结构化JSON数据

最大优势是极大简化了文档操作——原本需要50行Python代码和多个库才能完成的任务，现在只需一条命令即可实现。跨平台支持macOS、Linux和Windows，适合开发者和AI代理使用。

主要讨论点：针对AI代理操作Office文档的工具开发，涉及技术路线选择、实用性评估和企业应用需求

不同观点：

• **技术标准派**：强调ECMA 376标准合规性对无头生成和处理的重要性，认为这是专业实现的基础（rcarmo、jbgt）

• **实用质疑派**：质疑专用工具的必要性 - 认为直接用Python/Claude Code可能在提示遵循度、视觉效果和token消耗方面更优；或认为LaTeX等替代方案更适合（allan_s、beepbooptheory）

• **企业问责派**：指出真正难点不在生成而在验证 - 企业文档需要引用、数据、格式、语义的验证机制，否则无法实际应用（StahlGuo）

• **替代方案派**：建议非交互场景用HTML转PDF方案，体验更好（pietz）

• **趋同观察派**：多位开发者注意到类似想法同时涌现，认为这是有趣的市场信号，同时也在开发类似工具（jbgt、topaztee）

补充讨论：评论中出现商标使用争议（neilv批评"Office"称呼不当）、功能细节咨询（Excel公式/宏处理、LibreOffice支持）以及对token优化价值的认可。整体反映出AI文档自动化工具正处于探索期，实现路径和应用价值仍存在分歧。

data.title: Show HN: Pulpie – Models for Cleaning the Web
data.author: snyy
data.article_summary:
Pulpie是一个用于从HTML页面提取主要内容的开源模型家族，实现了质量与成本的帕累托最优。其最小模型pulpie-orange-small仅有210M参数，在WebMainBench上达到0.862的ROUGE-5 F1分数，接近领先模型Dripper（0.864分），但参数量只有后者三分之一。

核心创新在于采用编码器架构，单次前向传播即可标记所有HTML块，使处理速度达到13.7页/秒（Dripper仅0.68页/秒）。清洗10亿网页的成本仅为7,900美元，是Dripper的二十分之一（159,000美元）。

这项技术解决了网页数据清洗的瓶颈问题——典型HTML页面70%内容为导航、广告等噪音。更清洁的数据可显著提升模型预训练质量和推理准确性。模型已在Hugging Face开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个网页内容提取工具的功能范围、适用场景及技术方案选择

不同观点：

• **功能探索派**：关注工具的多场景能力。有人询问是否支持图像/表格/Shadow DOM处理，是否适用于电商产品抓取，以及对JavaScript渲染页面的支持情况。核心关切是工具能否覆盖"模型阅读"、"媒体保留"、"数据提取"等不同需求

• **技术质疑派**：认为传统HTML转Markdown加CSS选择器的免费方案就足够，质疑付费服务的必要性。有技术背景用户分享10年前用随机森林模型的经验，指出简单的P标签和词数阈值在新闻网站就能达到90%准确率

• **实用主义派**：多位用户表示会直接应用到实际项目中（web-to-kindle应用、Whisperit内容导入等），更关注工具的即用性而非技术实现

补充讨论：有用户指出产品体验问题（Mozilla暗色主题下表现不佳）和图表设计缺陷（成本坐标轴未从零开始）。整体评论以积极反馈为主，但缺乏对技术质疑的正面回应，显示社区对"简单方案vs付费服务"这一核心问题仍有分歧。

48806575.article_content:
Research Â· field note
Pulpie: Pareto-Optimal Models for Cleaning the Web
Authors
Bhavnick Minhas, Shreyash Nigam
Affiliation
Feyn Labs
Published
June 25, 2026
Reading time
13 min
Contents
Weâre introducing Pulpie, a family of Pareto-optimal models for extracting main content from HTML pages.
Pulpie approaches SOTA extraction quality at one twentieth the cost.
Our smallest model,
pulpie-orange-small
, scores 0.862 ROUGE-5 F1 on WebMainBench. This matches Dripper, the leading extractor, which scores 0.864. Pulpieâs performance is despite it being a third the size: 210M parameters versus Dripperâs 600M.
The gains come from architecture. Pulpie is an encoder that labels every HTML block as content or boilerplate in a single forward pass. This also makes it fast.
On an NVIDIA L4 GPU,
pulpie-orange-small
processes 13.7 pages/sec against Dripperâs 0.68 pages/sec. At $0.39/hr for an L4 instance,
cleaning 1 billion pages costs $7,900 with Pulpie and $159,000 with Dripper.
Pulpie unlocks high quality web extraction at a scale impossible before. We expect this to benefit pre-training and context management.
Our models are open source and available on
Hugging Face
. See
Get started
for instructions.
Extraction is the bottleneck
Language models consume the web twice. First in pre-training, where they learn about the world. Then at inference, when they pull in relevant context. Both times the input is mostly noise. During discovery, we found 70% of the blocks on a typical HTML page hold boilerplate like navigation, ads, sidebars, and footers. Main content is only a small fraction of the page.
However, that fraction determines model quality on both ends.
AICC (
Ma et al., 2025
) measured the effect of cleaner extraction on pre-training. The team built two corpora from the same Common Crawl snapshot. One extracted content with heuristics. The other extracted it with a model-based parser. Everything else in the data pipeline remained equal. They then trained an identical model on each corpus.
The model trained on the model-extracted corpus scored 1.08 percentage points higher in average accuracy across 13 benchmarks. Since only extraction logic changed, we can attribute the gain entirely to having cleaner data.
Impressively, the same model also beat models trained on FineWeb and RefinedWeb, two of the most heavily filtered pre-training corpora. These datasets have earned their reputations through elaborate filtering and deduplication. Beating them by improving the extractor illustrates the high value of clean data.
Beyond setting a low baseline, poor extraction materially harms models. Heuristics break structured content. The table below shows how Trafilatura and model-based extractors compare on preserving code blocks and formulas. Low similarity scores indicate corruption. If used in training, resulting models will inherit this damage.

Data quality matters at inference too.
Shi et al. (ICML 2023)
showed that a single irrelevant passage is enough to derail a modelâs answer. A model is more accurate and more efficient when its context is free of noise.
Cleaning on a budget
Cleaning the web pays off in both training and inference. The open question is how do we clean well at scale?
First, to understand the landscape, we can divide current extractors into two families based on the question: Does the method read the page, or inspect its structure?
Structure-based extractors
judge an HTML block by surface signals. They apply rules over tags, DOM, and text density to separate content from boilerplate. Trafilatura, Readability, and magic-html work this way. Boilerpipe goes one step further and trains a classifier on those same signals. These extractors are easy to run but they confuse similarly built elements. A navigation table and a data table look identical to an algorithm counting cells.
Reading extractors
feed the page to a transformer and label each block based on its content. Dripper is a decoder built on this idea. The decoder emits labels one token at a time. Each label forces the full model to be read from memory for a single step of work. This ties speed to memory bandwidth and makes runs expensive.
Pulpie keeps the reading approach but moves the bottleneck to compute. We do this by using an encoder architecture that labels every block in a single forward pass. This enables Pulpie to match Dripperâs quality while being smaller, faster, and cheaper.

data.title: Nintendo announces new product revisions in Europe with replaceable batteries
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary:
任天堂宣布从2026年夏季起，为应对2027年2月欧洲电池新规，将在欧洲市场逐步推出配备用户可更换电池的产品修订版。修订版产品功能与现有版本完全相同。

具体时间表：
- Joy-Con手柄（部分颜色）：2026年夏季起
- Nintendo Switch 2主机：2026年秋季
- Joy-Con 2及Pro手柄：2026年冬季
- N64和GameCube手柄：2027年初

修订版产品的电池容量和重量略有调整，例如Switch 2主机电池容量减少约1%，重量增加约10克。各产品的电池更换套件将在欧洲任天堂商店销售。修订版产品在欧洲各国的上市时间可能因制造和配送等因素而有所不同。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** EU强制要求用户可更换电池的新规定对任天堂Switch产品线的影响，以及该政策的利弊权衡

**不同观点：**

• **强烈支持派**：认为厂商本来就有能力实现可更换电池，只是缺乏动力。有用户举例UK版电动牙刷因EU规定而采用更高质量电池，设备续航和体验都更好。多位评论者赞赏"布鲁塞尔效应"推动全球产品改进

• **技术权衡派**：担心可更换电池设计会牺牲产品性能，比如需要增加开口、降低防水性能、减少1%容量或刚性。认为用螺丝固定的方案是可接受的折中

• **时机质疑派**：指出规定出台时机不佳，因为电池技术正在快速进步，固态电池预计2027年量产，届时电池寿命可能超过设备本身使用周期，使可更换需求降低

• **商业影响派**：分析任天堂将在2027年2月停售Switch一代产品，损失约15%硬件收入，可能加速Switch 2 Lite版本开发以填补市场空缺

**补充讨论：**

多位评论者好奇任天堂为何不在全球市场统一采用可更换电池版本，认为这是产品升级而非妥协。也有人关注维护两套SKU的成本问题。此外有评论指出任天堂将EOL信息埋在FAQ中缺乏透明度

data.title: Apricot Computers: An underrated British brand
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讲述了英国电脑品牌Apricot的兴衰历程。1990年BBC节目《Trouble Shooter》记录了Apricot在1989年面临的困境。

Apricot曾是首家推出486电脑的公司，同时生产Microchannel和AT架构机型，坚持在英国本土设计和制造。但作为小公司，它在与IBM等巨头的竞争中陷入困境：产品线过于庞大、研发成本高昂、硬件制造不盈利，只有维护和软件业务赚钱。

顾问Harvey-Jones指出，Apricot无法通过提高价格竞争，必须以更低价格提供更多功能。最终创始人Foster决定转向软件和维护业务，并为制造部门寻找战略合作伙伴。1999年6月30日，Apricot关闭苏格兰工厂，品牌落幕。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：**
90年代英国计算机品牌Apricot的历史评价，核心聚焦于其技术特点、市场定位和IBM PC兼容性问题。

**不同观点：**

• **怀旧派/正面评价**：多位用户回忆起在政府项目、PCB制造等场景中使用Apricot的积极体验。认为机器设计出众（键盘LCD显示屏等创新设计），BYTE杂志曾正面评测其486机型，在当时是优质产品。

• **技术批判派**：指出Apricot的致命缺陷——只实现DOS兼容而非完整的IBM PC兼容性，导致软件生态受限。关键论点：Apricot误判了市场方向，以为软件会像CP/M时代那样为不同硬件重新编译，但1984年后"运行DOS"实际意味着必须逐位克隆IBM BIOS。尽管架构更清洁，但无法运行主流软件使其边缘化。

• **简单否定派**：直接评价"很差"（pants），未提供详细论据。

**补充讨论：**
评论中穿插了对其他英国品牌（Elonex、Grid）的提及，以及对Glenrothes制造基地的讽刺性评论。有人询问Apricot相关企业（ACT、Misys、Finastra）的延续情况。争议焦点在于产品质量评价与商业策略失误的区分——即使产品本身不错，兼容性策略错误导致市场失败。

Dave Farquhar
Retro Computing
June 30, 2026
June 30, 2026
3 Comments
You hear a lot about Sinclair and Amstrad and Acorn computers. But when it comes to British brands, it seems like we don’t hear a lot about Apricot. But thanks to a television program that aired in early 1990, we know a fair bit about Apricot’s triumphs and struggles in the highly competitive PC market of the 1980s and 90s. It was on June 30, 1999 that Apricot closed its factory in Scotland and wound down its brand.
Apricot had an extensive line of computers in 1989. Each machine came in either AT architecture or Microchannel.
I have to give credit to longtime reader Gary Osborne for alerting me to the existence of this TV show. In the early 1990s, the BBC had a TV series called
Trouble Shooter
. In it, Sir John Harvey-Jones visits troubled manufacturing businesses and helps uncover and solve their problems. It reminds me in some ways of the modern TV series
Kitchen Nightmares
, where Gordon Ramsay visits restaurants and tries to turn them around in a week, except these weren’t restaurants. In episode 3 of Trouble Shooter, Harvey-Jones visited Apricot Computers in mid-1989. The episode aired in 1990. Thanks to that TV episode, we know more about Apricot’s inner workings than we do about the typical 1980s and 90s PC clone manufacturer.
What was Apricot Computers?
Apricot was an interesting computer company. They were the
first company to ship a 486-based PC in 1989
. Arguably that’s not quite as noteworthy as being the
first to ship a 386-based PC
, but they still beat all the big names in shipping a 486, including Compaq and IBM. Apricot was also noteworthy in licensing Microchannel from IBM. While Tandy and Dell announced Microchannel PCs, Apricot actually shipped them in quantity and stuck with the architecture for several years, selling them alongside conventional AT designs rather than choosing one or the other. And Apricot was interesting in that they bucked outsourcing design and manufacturing to Asia longer than many PC makers did. They designed their PCs in Birmingham, England, and manufactured them in Glenrothes, Scotland.
The challenges Apricot faced were not at all unlike the challenges companies attempting to design and build computers in the United States circa 1989 faced. It was much cheaper to build computers in Asia. And it was increasingly cheaper to outsource the design too. In that sense, Apricot’s struggles designing and building computers in the UK didn’t seem at all unfamiliar to me.
Apricot on Trouble Shooter
Harvey-Jones described Apricot’s problem as a minnow trying to swim with large multinational whales and sharks.
Apricot’s founder, Roger Foster, said the maintenance was the most profitable side of the business, but that it existed because Apricot sold hardware. The hardware side was not profitable. Harvey-Jones then turned to see if the software side of Apricot’s business, which was also profitable, relied on the hardware manufacturing. Of course, he found it didn’t. Apricot’s software ran on other IBM PC-compatible systems too.
The problems with UK-based design and manufacturing
What Harvey-Jones found was that research and development was expensive, and it fed into the hardware manufacturing, but not into the software or maintenance sides of the business. Harvey-Jones’s idea was to raise prices to cover the overhead and raise profits. When that proved a nonstarter, he visited the factory to see if cost reduction might be possible.
As he entered the factory, Harvey-Jones encountered a display of Apricot computers. He asked if that was the historical progression of the product line. An unnamed Apricot employee said no, it was the current product line.
He was audibly taken aback at the large number of models they produced. There were seven machines visible in the camera frame and the framing implied there were more machines out of frame. The employee said they produced both MCA and AT lines of computers. That subtle point is easy to miss. Apricot was making both Microchannel PCs, like IBM, and ISA-based AT machines like Compaq and
everyone else
.
Letting go
Harvey-Jones visited trade shows and talked to experts outside the company to try to get an understanding of the industry. Guy Kewney, a computer journalist, said you can’t compete with IBM by offering more at the same price. You have to offer more at a lower price, because of compatibility. He said he’d been talking to five different users of clone machines who were running into compatibility issues, so you have to save a significant amount of money to be willing to go through that.
The show ended with Foster concluding that Apricot needed to shift its emphasis to software and maintenance, and making an acquisition to shore up that side of the business and setting up a new company, ACT, toward that end. data.title: Eternal Software Initiative Based on Subleq One-Instruction-Set Computer
data.author: lioeters
data.article_summary:
这是Eternal Software Initiative（永恒软件计划）的GitHub仓库。该项目旨在解决软件的"比特腐烂"问题，确保当代软件能在遥远未来仍可运行。

核心方案：
1. 定义了一个极简的机器架构（基于Subleq OISC修改），简单到可以写在餐巾纸上，却足够强大
2. 提供完整工具链，包括LLVM编译器后端、Linux移植版、C/C++运行时库等
3. 可将现有软件编译成自包含的"capsule"（胶囊）

与QEMU等模拟器不同，ESI不依赖专有硬件或复杂软件栈。只要保存capsule二进制文件和餐巾纸上的架构说明，未来的历史学家或开发者就能重现今天的软件，无需了解当代计算机系统的任何知识。仓库包含参考虚拟机实现（约50行C代码）和完整构建说明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"永恒软件"（Eternal Software）保存方案及SUBLEQ虚拟机架构的可行性和局限性

不同观点：

• **技术自举派（anthk）**：认为应该通过cproc/cparser等工具实现系统自举（从自身编译内核、busybox等），但指出目前只有clang能充分编译Linux内核，暗示GCC可能不够理想

• **规范完整性质疑（curtisblaine）**：指出当前技术规范存在歧义 - 当A和B同时为-1时如何处理？"读取按键"是等待输入还是立即检查？如果等待，"无按键"是否意味着超时？这些细节未明确定义

• **实用性批判派（groby_b）**：提出根本性质疑 - 该方案假设的应用场景（未来文明想运行200年前软件）不现实；更重要的是，SUBLEQ虚拟机无法复现真实硬件环境（时序特性、未文档化的副作用、OS bug兼容性、I/O设备特性等），大多数软件依赖这些底层细节，单纯的"数字列表"无法解决；认为这更适合"从零引导计算"而非软件保存

• **基本假设质疑（mcphage）**：认为文档中"发现21世纪钛合金胶囊"的前提假设本身就不合理

补充讨论：核心争议在于抽象层次与实际依赖的矛盾 - 理想化的虚拟机架构与软件对具体硬件/系统环境的深度耦合之间存在鸿沟。

Introduction
This is the root repository for the
Eternal Software Initiative
.
The ESI defines a minimal machine architecture (based on a modification of the Subleq OISC) that is so simple that its complete specification can be
written down on a napkin
. We then provide an LLVM compiler backend for this architecture, a port of Linux, ports of the C/C++ runtime libraries, and other tools (including a
reference virtual machine implementation
in ~50 lines of C) required to build and run a self-contained 'capsule' from existing software.
What's the point of all this? Running today's software requires a complex stack of dependencies (compilers, libraries, frameworks, OS) on top of proprietary and incompletely documented hardware, making it very difficult to ensure that today's software will continue to operate in the future. This problem of 'bit rot' is well known to anyone maintaining legacy software over a timespan of years or decades, but now imagine a historian 1,000 years from now trying to understand 21st century life, much of which is experienced through software. Even if today's software binaries are preserved, it is far fetched to imagine those binaries will still be runnable. Emulators like QEMU move this problem around but do not solve it: they too have a similarly complex stack of software and hardware dependencies, and so also won't be runnable in the far future.
The ESI solves this problem by (1) defining an architecture that is simple enough to
write down on a napkin
but powerful enough to efficiently represent any software, but does not require knowledge of any proprietary hardware, software, frameworks and so forth, and (2) implementing a toolchain to compile any existing software into a self-contained 'capsule' for this architecture. This ensures that, providing the capsule binary and the napkin instructions are preserved, the software can be revived and experienced in the far future without assuming any knowledge of present day computing systems.
This repository includes everything needed to build and run your own ESI machine, and build ESI 'capsules' from existing software.
For more information on the ESI's mission, see:
https://www.eternal-software.org
Check Out
This repository includes, as submodules, ESI forks of the LLVM toolchain, the Linux kernel, uClibc-ng, and Busybox. These must all be checked out together.
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/adriancable/eternal
Build VM and Try It
You will need SDL3 to build the ESI virtual machine. Install with e.g.
apt install libsdl3-dev
. There are no other dependencies. SDL3 can easily be replaced with any other means for writing pixels and capturing keyboard events, now or in the future.
cd eternal/vm
make
xz -d ../capsules/vmlinux.bootimage.xz
./vm ../capsules/vmlinux.bootimage
When Linux has booted, try for example:
cd doom
./doom
Building the Toolchain
The ESI toolchain should build on any Linux system with minimal effort. We have also successfully built on macOS, with
some modifications
. Make sure you have
gcc
,
python3
,
CMake
,
ninja
,
flex
,
bison
installed and operational.
Start in the checked-out
eternal
folder.
Step 1: Build ESI LLVM
rm -rf llvm-project/build && mkdir -p llvm-project/build
cmake -G Ninja -S llvm-project/llvm -B llvm-project/build -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS="clang;lld" -DLLVM_BUILD_TOOLS=ON -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="" -DLLVM_EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="Subleq" -DLLVM_DEFAULT_TARGET_TRIPLE="subleq-unknown-linux" -DLLVM_FORCE_VC_REPOSITORY="ESI" -DLLVM_FORCE_VC_REVISION=""
cd llvm-project/build
ninja llc clang llvm-mc lld llvm-objcopy llvm-ar llvm-ranlib llvm-nm llvm-readelf llvm-strip llvm-objdump
Step 2: Install Linux Kernel Headers
cd ../../linux
make ARCH=subleq \
CC=../llvm-project/build/bin/clang \
LD=../llvm-project/build/bin/ld.lld \
AR=../llvm-project/build/bin/llvm-ar \
NM=../llvm-project/build/bin/llvm-nm \
OBJCOPY=../llvm-project/build/bin/llvm-objcopy \
INSTALL_HDR_PATH=../runtime/sysroot/kernel-headers \
headers_install
Step 3: Build and Install ESI C Runtime (uClibc-ng)
cd ../uclibc-ng
make ARCH=subleq defconfig
make ARCH=subleq \

data.article_summary: Januscape (CVE-2026-53359) 是一个KVM/x86虚拟机逃逸漏洞,由Hyunwoo Kim发现。这是首个同时影响Intel和AMD架构的guest-to-host逃逸漏洞,属于KVM/x86 shadow MMU仿真中的use-after-free漏洞。该漏洞存在约16年(2010-2026),攻击者可通过客户机操作逃逸至宿主机,威胁支持嵌套虚拟化的多租户公有云(如GCP、AWS)。曾作为0-day成功利用于Google kvmCTF。影响包括:虚拟机逃逸导致宿主机瘫痪(DoS)或代码执行(RCE),以及在某些发行版上的本地提权。

主要讨论点：KVM嵌套虚拟化漏洞的严重性、影响范围及应对策略

不同观点：

• **技术复杂性观点**：嵌套虚拟化在x86架构上实现困难，L0层需要处理L2层的故障，增加了复杂性和历史上的不稳定性，建议公共VM主机不要启用此功能

• **漏洞严重性评估**：这是首个同时影响AMD和Intel的KVM guest-to-host漏洞，存在16年才被发现，非常危险。不仅威胁多租户VM提供商，也影响使用VM沙箱隔离不受信任代码的场景

• **系统设计质疑**：批评Linux将/dev/kvm设为全局可写(0666)的设计，使普通用户可利用此漏洞提权获得root权限

• **经济学角度**：认为虚拟化资源共享只在极低预算(0-200$/月)场景有意义，建议认真的项目直接使用专用服务器(200$/月起)，避免整类LPE漏洞风险

补充讨论：多位评论者关注缓解措施，如询问禁用嵌套虚拟化功能或使用特定QEMU参数是否能规避风险。也有调侃性评论暗示Xen相比KVM的优势。

Januscape: Guest-to-Host Escape in KVM/x86
Abstract
This document describes the
Januscape (CVE-2026-53359)
vulnerability discovered and reported by
Hyunwoo Kim (@v4bel)
. It is a KVM escape vulnerability that lets a guest escape to the host in a KVM/x86 environment. To the best of public knowledge, this is the first guest-to-host exploit research triggerable on both Intel and AMD rather than being limited to a single architecture.
Januscape is a use-after-free vulnerability in the
shadow MMU
emulation of KVM/x86. It can trigger the bug with guest-side actions alone to corrupt the host kernel's shadow page, and it can threaten the guest-host isolation of KVM/x86 hosts that accept untrusted guests and expose nested virtualization, particularly multi-tenant x86 public clouds (GCP, AWS, etc.).
In fact, Januscape was successfully used as a 0-day exploit in
Google kvmCTF
.
For the detailed technical information,
see here
.
Note
After reporting this vulnerability to
linux-distros@vs.openwall.org
, the agreed embargo has ended, so the exploit is posted to oss-security and this Januscape document is published. For the disclosure timeline, see the technical detail document.
PoC Structure
Running the PoC inside a guest VM can trigger a host kernel panic. A full escape exploit that works in a controlled environment also exists, but it is not released at this time and is planned to be released in the very distant future.
On distributions like RHEL,
/dev/kvm
is world-writable (
0666
), so an unprivileged user could also turn this vulnerability into a reliable LPE to root. That said, doing so would be like paying gold for garbage, so I won't bother covering it.
PoC Usage
Inside the guest VM, install the headers and build the module.
# sudo apt-get install -y build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r)
# make
Load the module inside the guest. KVM holds the raw VMX/SVM state, so unload it first. Load with no argument on Intel, and with amd=1 on AMD.
[Intel]
# sudo rmmod kvm_intel; sudo insmod poc.ko
[AMD]
# sudo rmmod kvm_amd; sudo insmod poc.ko amd=1
The race starts, and within seconds to minutes the host KVM panics.
[*] poc step 4/4: race live -- host DoS triggering
...
kernel BUG at arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c (pte_list_remove)
Comm: qemu-kvm
This PoC is intended to provide accurate information. Do not use it on systems you are not authorized to test.
Affected Versions
Januscape (CVE-2026-53359) covers the range from
2032a93d66fa (2010-08-01)
to
81ccda30b4e8 (2026-06-16)
.
In other words, this vulnerability lay dormant for about "16 years".
FAQ
What is the impact of this vulnerability?
There are two impacts in total:
KVM escape
: With guest-side actions alone, an attacker can compromise the host that runs their VM. For example, an attacker who has rented just a single instance on a public cloud could panic the host kernel to take down every other tenant VM on the same physical machine (DoS), or run code with root privilege on the host to take over the host and all the guests on it (RCE).
LPE
: On distributions such as RHEL,
/dev/kvm
is world-writable (
0666
), so an unprivileged user can also use this vulnerability as a reliable LPE to gain root.
Should I be worried?
If you operate an x86 KVM host that accepts multi-tenant guests and supports nested virtualization, or use an instance on top of one, check that the 81ccda30b4e8 patch is applied to the host kernel.
Are arm64-based KVM hosts also vulnerable?
No. The vulnerability is triggered only on the Intel and AMD architectures. That said, if you have not yet patched the previously published
ITScape (CVE-2026-46316)
, your arm64 hosts are also vulnerable, so apply the patch promptly.
Does this vulnerability occur in QEMU?
No. Unlike the commonly published QEMU escape vulnerabilities, Januscape occurs in in-kernel KVM, so it is triggered independently of QEMU's emulation. Because of this, it can also threaten large public clouds that implement and use their own virtualization stack.
Do I need root inside the guest VM?
Yes. Inserting the module requires guest kernel privilege. When you are allocated an instance on a public cloud, you usually have root on your own VM, so this is satisfied. In a scenario without guest root, it must be chained with an LPE such as
Dirty Frag
.

data.title: Linux on the Atari Jaguar
data.author: cakehonolulu
data.article_summary: Atari Jaguar是1993年发布的游戏机，号称64位但商业上失败。文章讨论在其上运行Linux的技术挑战：Jaguar使用Motorola 68000处理器，仅有2MB内存。移植Linux需要使用XIP技术将内核只读部分放在ROM卡带中、动态部分放在RAM中，以克服内存限制。还需实现UART串口输出和定时器来启动系统。这展示了Linux对老旧硬件的适配能力。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** 在资源极其受限的Atari Jaguar游戏机（68000处理器，2MB内存）上运行现代Linux内核的技术成就

**不同观点：**

• **技术成就派**：多数评论者（bni, nommuenjoyer, scrame, hogehoge51）认为这是令人印象深刻的工程壮举，尤其考虑到68000处理器的历史地位和硬件限制，内核维护者还提供了性能优化建议

• **完整性质疑派**：LogicFailsMe指出仅使用68000 CPU而不启用Jaguar的GPU和DSP，本质上只是"美化的Atari ST主机"，认为真正的挑战应该是让全部硬件工作

• **实用性存疑派**：boznz虽欣赏技术努力但表示不会尝试；coupdejarnac暗示这类项目25年前可能已有人做过，新意有限

• **展示方式争议**：chiffre01希望看到真实CRT显示输出而非模拟器截图，质疑项目的真实性展示

**补充讨论：** 
评论中延伸出68000处理器家族的历史讨论，hogehoge51强调其在ARM之前可能是部署最广的处理器架构；rob74指出文章遗漏了Atari ST这一重要68k平台；jdswain提出通过定制卡带扩展RAM的技术改进方向

48808663.article_content:
What in the tarnation is an Atari Jaguar?
Released in North America in November of 1993, the Atari Jaguar promised to be the new cool kid in the block thanks to it's (Highly debated) 64 bits of pure power.
The Atari Jaguar
The console itself ended up being a commercial disaster, even after the release of the CD addon, the Jaguar CD; which managed to sell even less units in a desperate attempt to try and compete with the Sony Playstation and the Sega Saturn.
The Atari Jaguar CD Add-on
Why in the tarnation Linux of all things?
Interestingly enough, to this day, Linux has architecture code for the 68000-family of processors. 68040, 68030, 68010... and even the original base 68000 processor. All neatly structured under
arch/m68k/
.
As a refresher, the Motorola 68000 was a CISC processor with mixed 16-32 bit capabilities (It's usually described as being 32-bit internally due to the register width length and 16-bit because the data bus was 16-bit, so 2-byte transfers at a time).
It had a 24-bit address bus, 2 to the power 24; thereabout a maximum of 16MBs of addressable memory.
It was released on 1979 to compete with the soon-to-be-released 16-bit CPUs of the era.
The Motorola 68000
Overall, it got lots of traction commercially; it ended up being incoporated in lots of popular commercial hardware. Biggest contenders are the original Macintosh (And Apple Lisa), the Commodore Amiga series of computers (With varying generations of the 68000), the Sega Genesis/Megadrive, the Neo-Geo AES, Plexus workstations... and the Jaguar.
Let's now address the elephant in the room, why Linux.
Well, it's easy;
because we can
(
-ish
).
jmp _linux?
Doing a bringup for a new 68000-based Linux port should be easy... right? Well... you're in for a good time.
As you may know (Or not), there's an extended thought that Linux requires an MMU to run (You know, being able to use virtual memory is a good thing if we want to run software w/o having day-long headaches).
Technically you are
kind of
right, but there's
uClinux
; which precisely makes this feasible. At some point it stopped being a downstream fork of Linux to become part of it; thankfully it's baked in for
m68k
(And well, the flat memory model and the rest of requirements you can imagine that an MMU-less system has).
Okay so, we enable all the required configuration flags on the Linux
menuconfig
(To basically tell it not to use an MMU and use the
Flat Memory model
), we compile and it should run right? Well yes... but no.
What actually jmp _linux involves
The Jaguar has 2 megabytes of RAM (Mapped at 0x000000), (up to) 6 megabytes of ROM (The cartridge, basically) mapped at 0x80000 and 2 custom ICs (Tom & Jerry, a "GPU" and a DSP) which are also memory-mapped.
The main hurdle we have is the memory footprint; while it's true that it's a good amount, it's still not infinite (We're talking megabytes, not
gigabytes
).
We basically need to find a way to try and optimize our RAM usage. We can do the easy things first, removing features from the kernel, disabling debug... the usual suspects; but we'll still probably have the issue where we can't load the kernel to RAM w/o going OOM (Heck, we're not even considering an initramfs at this point, which are also bulky).
Thankfully, Linux is smart enough to let us "split" the kernel in 2 separate memory regions. One can take advantage of the fact that we can store the read-only sections of it (Think,
.rodata
or
.text
) on the cartidge (The ROM) and the dynamic sections (
.data
or
.bss
) in RAM (Think,
XIP
;
eXecute-In-Place
).
Fortunately for us, it's a matter of telling it where we have the RAM, and where we have the ROM and it (Liunx) handles the relocations for us.
Cool, we can now fit Linux on the Jaguar and it should be able to execute... right? Well sure, you can try specifying the base of the kernel (Remember,
non-PIC
code) and loading it there and just doing a
jmp $80000
... but how do we know what is happening under the hood?
What Linux needs to boot
In the context of booting Linux, we need 2 things (At least, when doing the bringup):
Any type of output so we can see kernel messages
Any way to tick the system (A timer, basically)
The first requisite usually involves
ye' good ol'
UART. The Jaguar's DSP (Jerry) has TXD & RXD pins that (At least for booting Linux) can be repurposed to do serial output (If we ignore anything that has to do with sound). Writing a small console driver that bitbangs the pins is enough to start seeing some
earlyprintk
messages.
The second one, is a bit tougher. But we can basically use any of the 2 timers that the Jerry IC has; commercial games & software use them for sound-related tasks but we'll use them to basically enable Linux to calibrate and setup the scheduler and the systems that also depend on a
PIT
. It's useful that they can both trigger an interrupt on the Jerry itself but also on the 68000. We can basically override the board-specific init of the 68000 on Linux and designate that as the PIT that L

data.title: Pruning RAG context down to what the answer actually needs
data.author: emil_sorensen
data.article_summary:
Kapa 公司在其 RAG（检索增强生成）系统中增加了一个"剪枝"步骤来优化成本。他们发现检索到的文档中约三分之二对回答问题无用，却仍产生费用。

他们的解决方案是：在检索器和生成器之间加入一个小型、低成本的 LLM，让它审查问题和所有检索到的文档，丢弃不需要的部分。这个方法能：
- 删除约 68% 的上下文
- 保持 96% 的召回率  
- 净降低三分之一的查询成本

传统的重排序评分方法失败了，因为：1）评分不能跨查询校准；2）无法评估文档集合的整体相关性（某些文档单独看不相关，但与其他文档配合才能完整回答问题）。

他们的 LLM 剪枝器能同时查看问题和所有文档，对每个文档进行五级评分，从而准确判断哪些文档是回答所必需的。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** RAG系统中的检索、剪枝策略及上下文管理的技术实现与风险

**不同观点：**

• **术语精确性争议**（agentdev001）：认为"RAG"被误用，应使用"语义检索"或"向量搜索"等更精确术语，因为RAG概念范围更广，包含工具使用等功能

• **相关性剪枝的风险论**（StackOptimist，核心争议）：强烈质疑基于相关性的剪枝策略，指出它会丢失罕见但关键的信息（如药物禁忌、例外条款），建议采用按结构而非按得分剪枝，保留完整记录单元而非逐句删减

• **小模型能力质疑**（chimpanzee2）：不信任小型LLM作为剪枝器，认为会成为处理精心检索信息的"智力瓶颈"

• **上下文质量优于数量**（Avery29）：指出不相关上下文反而会降低答案质量，支持剪枝必要性

• **资源效率考量**（wolvoleo）：强调上下文对能源消耗和处理时间的敏感性，从成本角度支持剪枝

**补充讨论：**
grewil2怀疑文章本身可能AI生成；alansaber建议与Claude代理对比；Imanari询问Pruner替代Reranker的可行性；esafak总结了使用李克特量表评分的技术方法。争议焦点在于：如何在节省资源和保留关键信息之间取得平衡。

48809354.article_content:
Jul 2, 2026
How we taught a small LLM to throw away 68% of our RAG context
Pruning agent context down to what the answer actually needs, while keeping 96% of recall
by
Lars Baltensperger
Kapa builds AI assistants that answer complex questions over large product knowledge bases. Think technical documentation, API references, PDFs, forums, support threads. Developers use our retrieval API to give their agents context about their product, and the same retrieval layer powers our end-to-end assistants.
For all the debate in 2026 about whether agents still need RAG, in our domain nothing comes close when knowledge bases get large and complex. Our retrieval comes in several forms, some agentic, some single-pass, but they all share the same shape: a retriever, which finds the chunks of documentation relevant to a question, and a generator, the LLM that writes the answer from them.
The short version of this post: we added a third step between the two. A small, cheap LLM reads the question and all the retrieved chunks together, and throws out the chunks the answer will not need before the expensive model ever sees them. It drops about 68% of the context, keeps about 96% of recall, and cuts the cost of a query by a third, net of its own cost. This post explains how we got there.
Ignored chunks still cost money
A retriever is a funnel. Embedding and keyword search cut a knowledge base of hundreds of thousands of chunks down to a few hundred candidates, a reranker orders them, and the top 15 or so reach the generator, the largest and most expensive model in the chain. Even then, most of what the generator reads is not needed for the question. That is deliberate: retrievers aim for maximum recall and trust the generator to ignore the noise.
But the generator is billed for every chunk it ignores. In our assistants, retrieved chunks are about two-thirds of the cost of a query, more than the answer, the conversation history, and the system prompt combined. Every chunk fewer cuts the query cost by about 4%. And in an agent, every tool call pours its output into the same context, so the context grows quickly; a tighter retrieval result buys room for everything else the agent has to hold and leaves less context to rot.
The catch is recall. Drop a chunk the answer needed and you traded a few cents for a wrong answer. A pruner is exactly as good as that tradeoff: compression gained per point of recall lost.
The obvious fix does not work
We already rerank before returning the top K, so we are sometimes asked to just expose the rerank scores and let callers cut on them: keep everything above 0.7, drop the rest. It fails for two reasons, and the second shaped everything we built.
First, a rerank score is an ordering, not a measurement. It says chunk A beats chunk B on this query, nothing more. The scores are not calibrated across queries,
Cohere too
says as much, so no fixed cutoff works. The only cutoff a ranking supports is positional, top-N, and that drops the last chunk whether it is noise or the answer.
Second, and this survives even perfect calibration: relevance is not a property of a single chunk. The rerankers in most pipelines are pointwise cross-encoders. They score each query-chunk pair alone, never alongside the other chunks it was retrieved with. Here is an anonymized production example:
The second chunk never mentions audit logs, so it scores as noise, yet it is half the answer, and no pointwise score can see that, because the chunk is only relevant next to the first one. Chunks also split multi-part questions between them, each useless alone. The real question is never whether a chunk is relevant by itself, but whether it belongs to a set that together answers the question.
A clever fix that fails the same way
Before giving up on the reranker we tried anchor documents (
Sinhababu et al.
): make the reranker's scale absolute by planting synthetic chunks of known relevance into the ranking, one written per level from Essential to Unrelated, then drop every real chunk that ranks below the anchor of the lowest level you want to keep. One extra LLM call on top of a rerank you already run, and genuinely elegant.
It did not work, for the same underlying reason. Anchors fix calibration, but they cannot fix the scores, and the reranker kept placing partially and indirectly relevant chunks below plainly irrelevant ones. To keep them, the anchor has to sit so low that hardly anything gets pruned.
That failure was the useful result: whatever prunes has to see the question and all the chunks at once, because the thing being judged is the set.
So we let an LLM grade the chunks
What we shipped is one listwise LLM call between the reranker and the generator. It gets the question and all the chunks, and grades every chunk against a five-level scale written into its prompt:
LLM Score
Level
Meaning
5
ESSENTIAL
The answer cannot be produced without this chunk, whether it answers directly or is a definition or prerequisite another chunk
48809354.article_summary:
Kapa 公司在其 RAG（检索增强生成）系统中增加了一个"剪枝"步骤来优化成本。他们发现检索到的文档中约三分之二对回答问题无用，却仍产生费用。

他们的解决方案是：在检索器和生成器之间加入一个小型、低成本的 LLM，让它审查问题和所有检索到的文档，丢弃不需要的部分。这个方法能：
- 删除约 68% 的上下文
- 保持 96% 的召回率  
- 净降低三分之一的查询成本

传统的重排序评分方法失败了，因为：1）评分不能跨查询校准；2）无法评估文档集合的整体相关性（某些文档单独看不相关，但与其他文档配合才能完整回答问题）。

他们的 LLM 剪枝器能同时查看问题和所有文档，对每个文档进行五级评分，从而准确判断哪些文档是回答所必需的。
48809354.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** RAG系统中的检索、剪枝策略及上下文管理的技术实现与风险

**不同观点：**

• **术语精确性争议**（agentdev001）：认为"RAG"被误用，应使用"语义检索"或"向量搜索"等更精确术语，因为RAG概念范围更广，包含工具使用等功能

• **相关性剪枝的风险论**（StackOptimist，核心争议）：强烈质疑基于相关性的剪枝策略，指出它会丢失罕见但关键的信息（如药物禁忌、例外条款），建议采用按结构而非按得分剪枝，保留完整记录单元而非逐句删减

• **小模型能力质疑**（chimpanzee2）：不信任小型LLM作为剪枝器，认为会成为处理精心检索信息的"智力瓶颈"

• **上下文质量优于数量**（Avery29）：指出不相关上下文反而会降低答案质量，支持剪枝必要性

• **资源效率考量**（wolvoleo）：强调上下文对能源消耗和处理时间的敏感性，从成本角度支持剪枝

**补充讨论：**
grewil2怀疑文章本身可能AI生成；alansaber建议与Claude代理对比；Imanari询问Pruner替代Reranker的可行性；esafak总结了使用李克特量表评分的技术方法。争议焦点在于：如何在节省资源和保留关键信息之间取得平衡。

data.title: Rotman Lens
data.author: thomasjb
data.article_summary:
罗特曼透镜（Rotman lens）是一种用于射频波束形成的无源电子元件，由Walter Rotman和R. F. Turner于1963年提出并获得专利。

该元件的核心优势是无需移相器即可形成多个天线波束。它包含多个输入端口（波束端口）和输出端口（阵列端口）。当信号从某个输入端口输入时，会以不同的相位偏移到达各个输出端口。将输出端口连接到天线阵列后，通过切换输入端口即可改变波束方向。

设计中可添加虚拟端口来吸收反射场。罗特曼透镜可采用空心波导或微带线/带状线基板制造，广泛应用于雷达系统的波束形成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rotman Lens（罗特曼透镜）这种天线波束成形技术的工作原理、应用场景和现代替代方案

不同观点：

• **技术演进派**：认为虽然Rotman Lens设计精巧，但现代全数字相控阵已经更便宜、更灵活（go_artemis提出可用廉价的全数字相控阵替代）

• **经典工程派**：欣赏这种"看似简单却充满黑魔法"的模拟工程设计，认为是AI无法企及的老派智慧（po1nt称其为"魔法符文"，brcmthrowaway强调这是Claude做不到的）

• **实用主义派**：关注具体应用问题——询问被动相移相比数字相移的优势何在，是否主要用于补偿天线几何差异而无需改变信号发生器（RossBencina的疑问）

• **技术好奇派**：想了解工作原理、制造难度、仿真工具等具体细节（amelius、ano-ther、bbminner的提问）

补充讨论：

• 多人注意到"nominative determinism"现象：发明者R.F. Turner的名字缩写恰好是"射频"

• 出现跨领域创意联想：有人想到用类似原理设计可调节的冲浪海浪

• 社区互助：有人分享了Lukas Henkel的可视化动画帮助理解，有人提议制作PCB封装便于使用

A

and R. F. Turner in 1963,

Beam, array and dummy ports on a Rotman lens
The component allows multiple antenna beams to be formed without the need for
phase shifters
. It consists of a range of input ports (also called beam ports) and output ports (also called array ports).

A signal applied to one of the input ports arrives at each of the output ports with a different
phase shift
. If the output ports are connected to individual antennas in an
antenna array
, this allows shaping the beam in different directions by switching which input port the signal is sent to.
[
4
]
So-called dummy ports can be added to the design, which are
terminated
to absorb fields that hit them, thus preventing reflections from the side wall of the lens.
[
3
]
[
5
]
Rotman lenses can be constructed either from hollow conductive
waveguides
or on a
stripline
or
microstrip
substrate. They are commonly used for beamforming in
radar
applications.

data.author: tosh

data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** LLVM编译器基础设施的优缺点及未来发展前景

**不同观点：**

• **优化能力不足派（tristenharr）：** 在设计Logos语言时发现，LLVM在处理强类型系统时错过大量潜在优化机会，暗示存在性能改进空间

• **编译速度悲观派（norir）：** 认为LLVM编译速度慢，在自动代码生成时代将成为严重瓶颈，预测未来5-10年市场份额会大幅下降，对LLVM技术前景非常悲观

• **可访问性乐观派（kelseyfrog）：** 强调LLVM对LLM（大语言模型）友好，使用LLVM生态系统可以快速构建自托管编译器，看好其易用性

• **历史视角派（pjmlp）：** 提醒关注LLVM之前的类似项目（如Amsterdam Compiler Toolkit、IBM PL.8），强调LLVM并非首创而是延续了编译器研究传统

**补充讨论：** 核心争议在于LLVM的技术局限性与实用价值之间的权衡——批评者关注性能瓶颈，支持者看重生态系统的成熟度和可访问性

data.title: M/PC – A Concatenative OS
data.author: caminanteblanco
data.article_summary: M/PC是一个为Varvara设计的连接式操作系统，灵感来自Openfirmware，用于在无文件浏览器环境下管理文件。它采用后缀表示法，函数位于操作数之后。系统通过屏幕顶部的单一提示符接受命令，文件可存储可重用的命令序列（使用波浪号前缀调用）。支持方向键和按键进行大部分无键盘操作。系统提供丰富的原语命令，包括文件操作（dir、mov、get、put、cpy、era、ren）、执行（run）、显示（icn、txt）、栈操作（pop、dup、swp、rot）和逻辑运算等，可实现完整的文件管理和系统控制功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个运行在64KB RAM硬件上的极简系统项目的技术特性、定位和设计理念

不同观点：

• **系统定位争议**：benj111认为这更像是一个shell而非操作系统，尽管项目自称为OS。他指出Unix管道本质上就是concatenative的，认为可以在这个方向上做更多探索

• **技术独特性质疑**：f47204表示困惑，不理解这个系统与传统命令行管道操作的本质区别在哪里

• **Forth语言影响**：benj111注意到系统中有大量Forth语言的元素（如dup, over, rot等栈操作），但对Forth式的"在栈中传递参数"的方式是否适合shell环境表示怀疑

• **硬件约束特点**：mtdewcmu指出该系统运行在仅有64KB RAM的硬件上，这是一个重要的技术限制和设计约束

补充讨论：
评论中有人称赞开发者Devine Lu Linvega的高生产力，并分享了项目的最新更新。另有提醒注意命名与MPC（Multimedia PC）的混淆问题。整体氛围是技术讨论，焦点在于这个极简系统的设计哲学、与传统Unix工具的关系，以及concatenative编程范式在shell环境中的应用可行性。

48809810.article_content:
•/PC
M/PC is a
concatenative
operating system for
Varvara
, inspired by
Openfirmware
, designed to manage files on system without a file browser. It uses the postfix notation, meaning that the function success their operands:
( Get the number of bytes in folder/file_name )
folder/ file_name cat len dec
Files can store reusable sequences of commands, the tilde prefix includes the content of the file:
( Content of ./show-slide )
slide_ swp cat 3cx22.icn cat 1 icn
1 ~show-slide
The interface uses a single prompt at the top of the screen to input commands:
Controls
The operating system can be used largely without a keyboard to navigate folders and launch roms:
left/right
Navigate Stack
up/down
Scroll Stack
A
Evaluate Selected Symbol
B
Directory/Back
Kiosk
To start M/PC as a BIOS rom so that when the user presses
F4
, Varvara returns to the BIOS instead of triggering a reboot, launch with arguments:
uxnemu m_pc.rom orca.rom run
Wallpaper
On boot, M/PC will try and draw an
ICN file
named wallpaperWWxHH.icn, where
WW
is the width of the screen divided by 8 in hexadecimal, and
HH
the height.
Reference
Here is the list of all primitives:
dir
( -- [f] )
Put the file names in the current location on the stack.
mov
( path -- [f] )
Move the current location to current/path, then do dir.
now
( -- date time )
Puts the date Tue, 23 Jun 2026, and time 11:48:45 on the stack.
run
( f.rom -- ok )
Run the rom file, return with F4.
icn
( f.icn blend -- ok )
Draw an
icn file
with
blend
.
txt
( f.txt line -- ok )
Read a text file starting at line.
len
( f -- hex )
Put the length of a file in hexadecimal.
put
( body f -- ok )
Create a file with the content of body.
get
( f -- body )
Put the content of a file on the stack.
cpy
( fsrc fdst -- ok )
Copy the content of fsrc into fdst.
era
( f -- ok )
Erase file.
ren
( fsrc fdst -- ok )
Rename file fsrc into fdst.
pop
( a -- )
Pop symbol at the top of the stack.
dup
( a -- a a )
Duplication symbol at the top of the stack.
ovr
( a b -- a b a )
Copy second symbol to the top of the stack.
swp
( a b -- b a )
Pull the second symbol to top.
rot
( a b c -- b c a )
Pull the third symbol to top.
add
( a b -- a+b )
Push the sum of two symbols.
sub
( a b -- a-b )
Push the difference of two symbols.
dec
( hex -- dec )
Convert hexadecimal number to decimal.
hex
( dec -- hex )
Convert decimal number to hexadecimal.
cat
( a b -- ab )
Concatenate two symbols.
cmp
( a b -- bool )
Compare the names of two symbols.
and
( a b -- bool )
Put true if both symbols are true.
ora
( a b -- bool )
Put true if either symbol is true.
rsz
( width height -- )
Resize the screen, puts true if resize is supported by
Screen
.
out
( a -- )
Output symbol to
Console/write
.
bye
( -- )
Quit.

data.title: Companies hire more after AI adoption
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary:
Ramp经济实验室发布研究报告，分析了超过21,000家美国公司的数据，探讨AI对就业的影响。

**核心发现：**

高强度采用AI的公司在采用后两年内员工总数增长10%，入门级员工增长更快，达到12%。这些公司还增加了入门级员工在workforce中的占比。

**重要条件：**

只有高强度采用AI（前三个月每员工每月约30美元投入）才能看到显著效果。低强度采用者无明显变化。存在6-12个月的学习曲线，需要时间让AI实践在团队中传播。

**分布不均：**

AI采用集中在规模更大、工程导向更强、获得风投支持的快速增长公司。采用模式受资金来源和地理位置等网络因素影响，而非行业本身。

June 30, 2026
Companies hire more after AI adoption
Ara Kharazian
Lead Economist, Ramp
Dear Colleagues
: The most important economic question of the next decade is how AI will affect jobs. Everyone wants to write that paper. Until now, no one has had the right dataset, so existing research has relied on a combination of guesses, surveys, AI exposure scores, and self-interested punditry. In fact, a recent paper from Stanford said the ideal dataset would use “business spend data” and cited Ramp data specifically.
Today, we published our first working paper:
A New Look at AI’s Impact on Jobs
. It uses firm-level spend data from Ramp joined with workforce data collected by Revelio Labs. In a sample covering more than 21,000 U.S. firms, we find that companies that invest heavily in AI grow headcount 10% over the two years following adoption. Entry-level headcount grows 12%.
Read the full paper and explore the data from Ramp Economics Lab
here
. The rest of this letter will outline our key findings, plans for future research, and some of my thoughts on what that means for our economy.
Key Takeaways
Firms that adopt AI grow headcount 10.2% over the two years following adoption
, but these gains are entirely driven by high-intensity adopters. Low-intensity adopters see no statistically significant change.
Entry-level headcount grew even faster
. At the companies making the largest AI investments, entry-level headcount grew 12% over the two years following adoption.
AI adoption and the associated gains are unevenly distributed
. AI adopters are already larger, more engineering-intensive, more likely to be venture-backed, and faster-growing than non-adopters. These firms then grow faster upon adoption.
Do companies hire more after adopting AI?
Our main result says yes. Companies that use AI grow their headcount 10% over the two years following AI adoption. Two caveats to that:
AI adoption is subject to a minimum threshold:
You only see gains when you adopt AI with “high-intensity.” In our analysis, we defined high-intensity as firms in the top third of per-employee-per-month spend on AI in the first three months. That’s not necessarily the ideal way to describe great AI adoption, but it correlates with what I wanted to capture: these are the firms that spend on multiple models and use the most advanced and productivity-enhancing products available (coding agents and APIs as opposed to simple chat subscriptions). Note the top-third isn’t spending
that much
. About $30 per employee per month in the first three months, rising thereafter, but not
thousands of dollars.
The gains are subject to a learning curve
: Firms don’t increase their headcount until 6-12 months following adoption, and these gains compound over time. It takes time for best practices to proliferate through teams and individual and organizational workflows, before they change company operations enough to drive growth and affect hiring.
Entry-level headcount grows even faster
After we answered the first question, whether firms that adopted AI were hiring more, our paper shifted to answer: are they hiring differently? We tested several job categories and education-levels. Broadly, we found similar (at worst, net-neutral) growth across job functions, except for entry-level positions.
Entry-level hiring grew 12% in the high-intensity group. It grew so fast that at the end of the 24-month analysis period, firms in the high-intensity group also increased their workforce share of entry-level workers (up 1.15 percentage points compared to the control group).
It’s the first and only example we’ve seen so far that high-intensity AI firms are selecting different kinds of candidates. In this case, we believe they are selecting for a new set of skills, specifically, people who know how to use AI and use it well. Entry-level workers, especially recent graduates and college students, are a natural place to look.
These results are early, and we intend to track and update them over time, but it’s a promising (and intuitive) result for young people who have gotten seemingly exclusively negative news about their job prospects in recent years. I have seen it firsthand from hiring managers we spoke to in developing early versions of this paper.
The Gains from AI Are Unevenly Distributed
A side-result of this paper is that we found that AI proliferates through networks, and those networks can lead to outcomes that are economically suboptimal.
For example, who funded you is a better predictor of AI adoption than the sector you’re in. VC-backed companies of any kind are more likely to use AI, and use it intensely, than legacy tech companies. There’s also proliferation around who you know and the places you hire from. California-based tech companies are more likely to use AI than similar companies in New York. There’s no inherent reason for

data.title: Ternlight – 7 MB embedding model that runs in browser (WASM)
data.author: soycaporal
data.article_summary: 这是一个名为 @ternlight/mini 的轻量级嵌入模型系统界面。它使用三值化（ternary）BitLinear 技术，可在 CPU 上运行 Transformer 模型。界面显示了模型加载状态、嵌入延迟、吞吐量等性能指标。系统支持组件间状态共享、优化重渲染、避免属性钻取等功能。采用 MIT 开源协议，首次加载后可缓存，无需网络请求。这是一个面向 Web 开发的本地运行嵌入模型工具包。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：** 浏览器端运行的小型嵌入模型的实用性、应用场景及潜在问题

**不同观点：**

• **积极支持派**：认为本地嵌入模型带来隐私保护和无API依赖的优势，适用于产品搜索、FAQ匹配等场景。多位开发者分享了类似项目经验（ONNX+Transformers.js、离线搜索引擎、BERT Hash等）

• **应用扩展派**：建议将技术整合到元框架（如Astro）实现静态向量搜索，或与duckdb HNSW结合构建开放的分布式搜索生态系统，摆脱大公司控制

• **性能优化派**：指出打开网页时CPU占用高导致风扇疯转，建议添加触发按钮；询问能否预先完成嵌入计算以提升用户体验

• **隐私担忧派**：警告这可能被滥用——网站强制推送LLM到浏览器，占用用户CPU进行数据分析，侵犯隐私

• **标准化倡议派**：认为需要W3C制定LLM API标准（类似Chrome现有API），避免碎片化和滥用

**补充讨论：** 技术路线上有WASM优于JavaScript的认可；模型选择上提到Granite r2 small（30M参数）可作为微调基准；整体氛围积极，但隐私保护与潜在滥用形成核心争议点

data.title: How to sequence your own DNA at home
data.author: bilsbie
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了作者在家中对自己基因组进行测序的经历。作者使用Oxford Nanopore MinION设备（售价7500美元）已完成5次个人基因组测序，从采集口腔拭子细胞、样本制备、测序到数据分析全流程自主完成。

整个准备过程耗时约两个月，需要购买实验室设备（离心机、加热器等）、消耗品和试剂。虽然成本目前仍较高，但正在快速下降。获得基因组数据后，可通过VEP、ClinVar、PharmGKB等工具分析基因变异、药物代谢差异和罕见突变。

作者强调，目前的分析结果尚未达到临床诊断水平，不应盲目进行基因编辑。文章详细列出了所需硬件、试剂、软件和完整实验流程，可供AI辅助指导操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家庭DNA测序技术的可行性、隐私安全与伦理风险

不同观点：

• **支持与兴奋派**：认为技术令人振奋，掌上设备即可测序是巨大进步，期待开源基因共享平台和各种创新应用（如下水道根系检测、狗粪便追踪罚款）

• **成本质疑派**：认为$7.5k设备过于昂贵，建议等待降价或使用更便宜的第三方服务（$599商业方案）

• **专业警告派**（mjg59，具有博士背景）：强调湿实验室操作难度高、失败率高、环境要求严格，数据准确性存疑，基因数据解读必须由专业遗传咨询师完成，严重反对使用LLM进行基因解读

• **隐私矛盾派**：指出建立家庭实验室是为了隐私，却要将数据上传到云端LLM分析，这一矛盾未解决。关注是否有完全本地运行的开源分析工具

• **生物安全担忧派**：警告家庭生物技术可能导致DIY病毒制造，与AI、气候变化并列为三大反乌托邦威胁；担心CRISPR家庭化带来《千钧一发》式的伦理问题

补充讨论：多位评论者质疑实际结果的准确性和可用性，希望看到真实数据表现；对AI辅助实验的说法表示困惑

48812156.article_content:
How to sequence your own DNA at home
I have now sequenced my own genome 5 times with an
Oxford Nanopore Technologies MinION
. This means collecting them from a swab, prepping them for sequencing, running them through a sequencer, then doing analysis over them.
Cheek cells are easily accessible and replenish pretty quickly. They are not used for cancer diagnosis, inflammation, or what genes are being activated in other parts of the body (like if you have hives on your chest and want to test what genes are being expressed in the cells that are inflamed), since you would want to collect the cells having problems and compare them against other normal versions of those cells.
To sequence the cells, I bought lab materials and consumables to sequence my own genome at home. It took me about two months to get everything together to do a full end to end high quality run. Likewise,
the costs are still out of reach for the average person
but they are decreasing (exponentially!) and we will eventually have affordable technology, like a cell phone or AI, telling us about our DNA + RNA expression real-time.
What can I even do with my own genome?
Before we actually spend all this time and money on sequencing, what can we
actually do
with our genome?
The genome is not magic by itself- it is the reference layer. Once I have a VCF, I can run it through tools like
VEP
,
ClinVar
,
gnomAD
,
PharmGKB
(highly recommend),
Gene Inspector
, or Claude, and start asking:
Which variants do I have?
Which genes and pathways are affected?
Which medicines might I metabolize differently?
What rare variants should I take seriously?
Where does the model know nothing yet?
This last part matters- the information produced is not yet diagnosis-level, and it is definitely not “edit yourself with CRISPR because an AI said so.” The near-term value is turning a static genome into something queryable, but the “edit yourself with CRISPR” will most likely follow. DNA is the stable reference, RNA is the current state, and we will eventually integrate all biosensor data into one ‘model’ of yourself.
Here are a list of links and Twitter posts to help:
Genetic variants from first principles:
Adib @ ICML 🇰🇷
Adib @ ICML 🇰🇷 on Twitter / X
TLDR these genes, and the combinations of them, compound into real physical diseases. We will probably map these in the next decade
Pass your genome + RNA to any of these models:

Give your genome to Claude Code- message me if you want me to set this up for you

if you metabolize particular drugs differently
Patrick Collison post
on using agents to talk to his genome

主要讨论点：小型专业化AI模型（SLMs）在离线场景和资源受限环境中的应用前景

不同观点：

• **支持SLMs发展派**：认为未来将出现大量超专业化的小模型，通过编排层协调实现通用智能，类似人脑的皮质柱分工机制。AGI不会从单纯训练更大的LLM中产生。有实践者分享了多年本地小模型开发经验，发布了近百个可本地运行的模型。

• **实用场景关注派**：强调SLMs在网络中断、硬件受限等特殊场景的价值，如应急救援包、弱硬件环境。有人探索神经符号AI方案——小模型处理对话，内置求解器处理复杂计算。

• **技术怀疑派**：质疑"AI"概念泛化，认为简单的数据库搜索不应被称为AI。另有观点认为随着Starlink等卫星网络普及，离线模型的需求会降低。

• **安全与技术问题**：有人担忧物联网设备的安全风险，也有人抱怨模型响应延迟和网络切换问题。

补充讨论：评论中出现具体产品询问（RxScanner药物扫描仪）和技术实现问题（无本地算力时的训练方法），反映出从理论到实践的关注跨度。

data.title: Full Writeup of the Windows GDID
data.author: typeofhuman
data.article_summary:
本文全面揭示了Windows"全局设备标识符"（GDID）的工作原理。GDID在2026年7月美国司法部起诉Scattered Spider黑客组织的案件中首次公开。

**核心发现：**
- GDID是64位的Microsoft Account设备PUID（格式为g:数字），而非网传的128位
- 不是从硬件序列号生成，因为重装系统会产生新GDID
- 技术路径：微软账户服务(wlidsvc)从login.live.com获取设备PUID → 存入注册表 → 连接设备平台(CDP)读取并注册到设备目录服务 → Delivery Optimization上报

**关键特征：**
持久性标识符，绑定Windows安装实例而非硬件，可通过注册表直接查看。文章基于法庭文件、实机测试和二进制逆向工程，逐条驳斥了社交媒体的错误传闻。
data.comments_summary:
**主要讨论点：**Windows GDID（全局设备ID）如何被FBI用于追踪黑客，以及这项技术的准确性和隐私影响

**不同观点：**

• **技术准确性争议**：maxo133强烈质疑原研究是"AI生成的不准确内容"，指出真正的GDID应该在注册表IrisService键中（以"g:"开头），而不是研究中声称的位置；还指出无需微软账户也会生成GDID

• **隐私和监控担忧**：stackghost担心这种监控会随年龄验证扩大范围，认为此遥测数据主要用于执法和广告追踪；xyst认为这是微软强推账户登录的真实原因

• **技术对抗性**：jcarrano讽刺用充满间谍软件的Windows 11进行网络犯罪很愚蠢；nullbio指出重装系统无用，硬件中嵌入了多种ID；gigel82补充说硬件哈希（包含SMBIOS、CPUID、TPM等）才是真正不可变的标识符

• **方法真实性质疑**：webgambit怀疑FBI是否真用此方法，或只是为隐藏其他侦查工具而声称使用GDID

**补充讨论：**
hyperrail澄清GDID自2015年Windows 10就公开存在（可在反馈中心查看）；多人询问技术细节如能否修改GDID、Mac是否有类似机制、如何关联浏览历史等；最核心争议是原研究的技术准确性问题。

Full writeup of the Windows GDID
Global Device Identifier fully reverse engineered
How Microsoft's "Global Device Identifier", the persistent Windows fingerprint named in the July 2026 Scattered Spider complaint, is actually generated, stored, and transmitted.
TL;DR
Note
Listed below is true, but missing some information. Regardless of being logged in with a MSA you WILL have a GDID. I didn't realize this at the time of posting but I looked into it. CDP has an anonymous device path that is used if no MSA has been connected. The underlying system is still factually correct just missing a few things.
GDID is a real telemetry item.
It shows up in the U.S. federal criminal complaint (
United States v. Peter Stokes
, N.D. Ill., July 2026) as
Global Device Identifier g:6755467234350028
.
It is a Microsoft Account "Device PUID".
A 64 bit Passport Unique ID assigned to a Windows installation when it registers with a Microsoft Account, written in the device graph as
g:<decimal>
.
The claims are wrong.
It is
not
"128 bit" and
not
"generated from serial numbers." The court record itself says a
reinstall produces a new GDID
, which rules out it being derived from hardware serials like your GPU.
The stack, bottom to top:
wlidsvc
(Microsoft Account service) provisions the device with
login.live.com
and gets back a device PUID -> stores it in the registry -> the Connected Devices Platform (
cdp.dll
/
CDPSvc
) reads it and registers it into the
Device Directory Service (DDS)
graph -> Delivery Optimization reports it as the documented
UCDOStatus.GlobalDeviceId
.
All of it was reproduced on a live Windows 11 (26200) machine with public symbols.
You can find your own GDID in one registry read
(
§7
).
Note
Confidence labelling.
Every claim is tagged so you can weigh each one yourself:
[COURT]
primary source fact,
[OBSERVED]
reproduced live on my test machine,
[STATIC]
proven from binaries and public Windows PDBs,
[ASSESSED]
strong inference from the evidence.
Contents
Background: what the court actually said
Debunking the viral myths
Where GDID surfaces: Delivery Optimization
Who owns it: Connected Devices Platform to DDS
How CDP gets it: it consumes, it does not compute
The mint: MSA Device PUID (
wlidsvc
)
Find your own GDID
Reducing the exposure
Methodology (reproducible)
Limitations and honest caveats
1. Background: what the court actually said
On July 1, 2026 the DOJ unsealed a criminal complaint against Peter Stokes, an alleged member of
Scattered Spider
(a.k.a. Octo Tempest / UNC3944 / 0ktapus). The affidavit describes how Microsoft helped the FBI attribute activity to a device.
Important
[COURT]
From the superseding complaint (¶25, p.34), verbatim:
"the ngrok account was set up through
Global Device Identifier g:6755467234350028
('the GDID'). According to a Microsoft representative, a Global Device Identifier in the Windows ecosystem is a
persistent, device level identifier designed to uniquely identify an installation of a Windows operating system
on a device... A GDID is a globally unique identifier tied to the
installation
of Windows on a device. A GDID remains consistent across Windows operating system updates on a device, but a
reinstall of Windows... will be tied to a new unique GDID.
"
A footnote adds that one Microsoft user can have multiple GDIDs. The affidavit then correlates the GDID's IP history and browsing (e.g.
empirehotelnyc.com
, a Growtopia/Ubisoft login URL) with the accounts the suspect was logged into.
Two things here carry the rest of this writeup:
The value is
g:
plus a decimal integer
(
g:6755467234350028
). In hex that is
0x0018000FC8CB93CC
, so a
64 bit
number.
A reinstall gives a new GDID.
So it can't just be a function of unchanging hardware.
2. Debunking the viral narrative
The social media summary claimed the GDID is
"a 128 bit identifier generated from serial numbers on install."
Both halves are false:
Claim (social media)
Reality (primary source)
"128 bit"
The value in the complaint is
g:6755467234350028
, a decimal that fits in
64 bits
(
0x0018000FC8CB93CC
).
"generated from serial numbers on install"
The complaint says a
reinstall produces a new GDID
. A value derived from fixed serials would come back the same after a reinstall, not change.
Note
After some more reversing of CDP. I provided some misinfo. Using a local account does not prevent a GDID. CDP has an anonymous device path that is taken if no microsoft account. Keep this in mind when reading.
3. Where GDID surfaces: Delivery Optimization
[STATIC]
Microsoft's public Azure Monitor docs define a
GlobalDeviceId
column in the
UCDOStatus
(Update Compliance / Delivery Optimization) table:
Gl

data.article_summary:
这不是一篇单独的文章，而是 cr.yp.to 博客的目录索引。该博客主要讨论密码学话题，特别是后量子密码学(PQ crypto)，涵盖2016-2026年的文章。核心内容包括：NSA和IETF标准化过程中的争议、NIST后量子密码标准的安全性分析、混合加密方案的辩论、Kyber和McEliece等算法的评估、以及对政府机构在加密标准制定中角色的批判性分析。作者关注标准化公平性、安全风险量化和技术实现细节。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于TLS中是否应该支持纯MLKEM（后量子密码）标准的激烈争议

不同观点：

• **支持纯MLKEM方：**认为MLKEM由欧洲知名学者设计（非NSA），已经过充分研究，与椭圆曲线密码学研究程度相当；多个标准组织（O-RAN、IEEE、3GPP）需要此RFC作为规范参考

• **反对纯MLKEM方（Bernstein领导）：**组织邮件列表投票反对，认为应该只允许混合方案（ECC+PQ）；质疑NSA历史上削弱密码标准的记录（如DES）；担心后量子算法尚不成熟

• **支持混合方案方（法德政府立场）：**明确表示后量子算法研究不足，侧信道攻击和实现安全性尚未充分验证，应在短中期内必须使用混合方案

• **程序公正性质疑：**批评Bernstein操纵投票流程，提供统一标题让支持者加入邮件列表投票；指出IETF共识不是简单数字投票

• **信任危机观点：**部分人完全不信任美国政府机构推荐的标准；有人担心NSA可能专门攻击混合方案以"推销"纯PQ方案

补充讨论：已发现Kyberslash漏洞暴露实现安全问题；即使RFC不通过IETF也可独立发布；Bernstein与NIST有历史纠纷（曾起诉NIST要求公开Kyber选择文件）

• **支持纯MLKEM方：**认为MLKEM由欧洲知名学者设计（非NSA），已经过充分研究，与椭圆曲线密码学研究程度相当；多个标准组织（O-RAN、IEEE、3GPP）需要此RFC作为规范参考

• **反对纯MLKEM方（Bernstein领导）：**组织邮件列表投票反对，认为应该只允许混合方案（ECC+PQ）；质疑NSA历史上削弱密码标准的记录（如DES）；担心后量子算法尚不成熟

• **支持混合方案方（法德政府立场）：**明确表示后量子算法研究不足，侧信道攻击和实现安全性尚未充分验证，应在短中期内必须使用混合方案

• **程序公正性质疑：**批评Bernstein操纵投票流程，提供统一标题让支持者加入邮件列表投票；指出IETF共识不是简单数字投票

• **信任危机观点：**部分人完全不信任美国政府机构推荐的标准；有人担心NSA可能专门攻击混合方案以"推销"纯PQ方案

补充讨论：已发现Kyberslash漏洞暴露实现安全问题；即使RFC不通过IETF也可独立发布；Bernstein与NIST有历史纠纷（曾起诉NIST要求公开Kyber选择文件）

data.title: Evaluation order and nontermination in query languages
data.author: luu
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论有限函数式编程（λFS）系统，该系统试图结合函数式编程与关系式编程（如Datalog/SQL）。在λFS中，关系被表示为有限函数，只有有限个输入返回非默认值，运行时用哈希表存储。

文章重点探讨递归和求值顺序的难题。关键问题是：在关系查询中，不同的求值顺序可能影响程序终止性。例如查询`Q(x) := R(x) and test(x) and S(x)`，可以先遍历R再检查S，或先求R、S交集再调用test。若test在某些输入上不终止，求值顺序将决定程序能否终止。

这暴露了数据库（强调查询优化）与编程语言（强调可组合推理）间的矛盾。文章提出三种可能方案，其中从左到右求值最简单，具有清晰的成本模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：程序求值顺序、查询规划与终止性问题

不同观点：
• **理论视角（mrkeen）**：强调Church-Rosser定理的重要性，指出原文未充分说明惰性求值的关键优势——如果存在终止路径，惰性求值（call-by-need）能够找到它，这比单纯提及合流性更有价值

• **实践视角（veqq）**：从实际开发角度出发，展示了灵活查询语言的设计——允许查询操作（where、group-by等）以任意顺序编写，同时提供宏机制让开发者在需要时精确控制执行顺序

• **文章解读（_alternator_）**：认为讨论核心是"有限程序中可能出现无界计算时的查询规划问题"，关注的是理论与实践的交叉点

补充讨论：评论间存在理论与实践的张力——mrkeen关注lambda演算的理论完备性，veqq展示了现实中如何平衡声明式编程的简洁性与执行控制的需求。eru推荐的Dhall语言可能是相关配置语言的参考实现。整体讨论围绕"求值顺序的灵活性与可预测性"这一核心矛盾展开。

48757619.article_content:
Last month I gave a talk at
FLOPS
about
finite functional programming
or ‘λFS’, my latest attempt (previously:
Datafun
) to combine functional programming with relational programming à la Datalog or SQL – and tensor algebra too, because why not?
In λFS, a relation R is treated as a function: we let R(
x
) = true iff
x
is in R, false otherwise. This function is
finite
in that
R(
x
) = true
for only finitely many inputs
x
: these are its
support.
The paper
gives a type system for ensuring functions have finite support. At runtime, we represent a finite boolean function by tabulating its support in a hash table or a balanced tree (like a table in a database).
This generalizes beyond booleans to any codomain with a ‘default’ value.
A function’s support are those inputs whose output is non-default; for instance, the booleans with false as default, or the integers with 0 as default.
A finite function can then be represented as a key-value table whose keys are the function’s support; any other key implicitly maps to the default value.
Non-boolean finite maps arise naturally as the result of aggregations, while tensor algebra is essentially relational algebra over non-boolean (usually real-valued) finite maps.
Nontermination and evaluation order
In the talk, I mentioned that recursion was future work for λFS. Naturally, someone – I think it was Atsushi Igarashi – asked what the difficulty was. The primary difficulty is that recursion allows nontermination. Semantics for nontermination usually use domain theory, which has fallen out of fashion in recent decades, and which consequently I’ve never deeply studied and find a bit intimidating.
1
Moreover, as soon as nontermination or any effect is involved, there is a question of evaluation order. Even in the untyped lambda calculus, where evaluation is confluent, call-by-name and call-by-value evaluation terminate on different programs. What’s worse, in relational languages ‘evaluation order’ has a more expansive meaning than in functional languages. Consider this example:
Given
R,S  : nat => bool
input tables
and
test : nat -> bool
a black-box predicate
let
Q(x) := R(x) and test(x) and S(x)
the query
Here,
=>
denotes a finite function, represented as a table, while
->
denotes an arbitrary function, represented by a procedure or closure.  Thinking relationally, our query
Q
is the intersection of the tables
R
and
S
, filtered by the black-box predicate
test
.
The central question is:
in what order do we evaluate this query?
We could go left-to-right: for each
x
in
R
, if
test(x)
passes, check if
x
is in
S
. In Python:
[x for x in R if test(x) if x in S]
Or, noting that
test
may be expensive but looking up an entry in a table is cheap, we could check if
x
is in
S
before calling
test
:
[x for x in R if x in S if test(x)]
And if we happen to know
S
is much smaller than
R
, we can save a lot of time by iterating over
S
instead of
R
:
[x for x in S if x in R if test(x)]
The standard relational philosophy regards evaluation order as an implementation detail, decided by the query planner. However, this ordering may affect whether
Q
terminates, because different orders call
test
on different arguments. A contrived example:
R := {"hello", "world"}
S := {"hello", "alice"}
test(x) := x == "hello" or loop-forever()
Q(x) := R(x) and test(x) and S(x)
Left-to-right execution calls
test("hello")
, which succeeds, followed by
test("world")
, which loops forever. But if we intersect
R
and
S
before
calling
test
, we only test
"hello"
and so terminate.
I have expressed this problem in λFS, but it arises in any SQL or Datalog engine supporting user-defined functions, and exposes a tension between typical DB and PL assumptions:
DB
The query engine may choose the execution strategy to optimize performance.
PL
We can reason compositionally about program behavior – in particular, about termination or execution time.
λFS tries to bridge DB and PL, and gets stuck in the awkward middle: I must either favor one perspective over another, or find a way to thread the needle’s eye. I do not yet know how best to do this. Instead, here are three directions forward – three sketches of possible semantics for λFS with recursion (or Datalog with nonterminating functions).
1
Left to right evaluation has a simple cost model
The simplest strategy to implement also has the most straightforward semantics: evaluate from left to right.
This is the most typical PL approach: it avoids query planning and puts the job squarely in the hands of the programmer.
This makes the execution time of a query easy to predict and reason about, as my friend
Rob Simmons
pointed out to me while working on
Finite Choice Logic Programming
; this is more or less the cost model of
Dusa
, an implementation of FCLP.
In this approach, a conjunction of
n
terms turns into at most
n
nested loops. For instance,
R(x) and S(y)
becomes 2 loops:
for x in R:
for y in S:
yield (x,y)

R(x) and S(x)

S(x)

data.title: Acronym Fatigue Series Introduction: why I'm wary of acronyms
data.author: DanielVZ
data.article_summary:
作者宣布推出"缩略语疲劳系列"(AFS)，探讨对技术领域缩略语过度使用的警惕。

他的谨慎态度源于两方面：**文化差异**——西班牙语母语背景下缩略语远不如英语普遍；**学术背景**——人文学科更倾向概念创造而非缩略语。

文章指出，英语使用者对缩略语情有独钟，这被科技营销大量利用。缩略语成为群体归属信号：懂的人觉得是"圈内人"，不懂的人则被排除在外。营销团队通过制造大量缩略语（包括公司自创的）来营造专业感。

作者的核心担忧是：**缩略语因其易记易传播的特性而流行，但这种传播力可能与其实际价值无关**。好记的首字母组合（如SOLID）本身就具有模因传播优势，这可能掩盖了概念本身的质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术和专业领域中缩写词的使用是否合理，以及如何平衡效率与可读性

不同观点：

• **支持派**：缩写词在专业领域必不可少，能提高沟通效率和信息密度。技术领域需要命名大量新概念，缩写词是自然选择（如 HTTP 比完整拼写更实用）。在特定受众中使用行业缩写词反而更清晰

• **反对派**：缩写词制造理解假象，总是以读者为代价。是作者懒惰和短视的表现，牺牲了长期可读性。特别批评不先介绍就直接使用缩写词的做法

• **文化批评**：美国军事文化导致缩写词过度使用，成为文化霸权的一部分。其他语言和文化较少依赖缩写词

• **实际问题**：不同领域使用相同缩写词造成混淆（如 LoRa vs LORA）；积累过多缩写词导致认知负担和语言不精确；a11y 等数字压缩形式难以解码

补充讨论：多数人认同缩写词本身不是问题，关键在于使用场景和方式。专业内部交流可接受，但面向公众时应谨慎。需要在效率和可读性之间找到平衡，并注意引入新缩写词时的规范性

..
2026-07-05
Acronym Fatigue Series Introduction: why I’m wary of acronyms
Published
2026-07-05T01:30:02Z
Daniel
In a
recent post
, I did a brief critique of what I called Acronym Marketing. It was so brief that it may have looked like it came from ignorance. But in reality after reflecting on it, I think it comes from two places: cultural differences and due to their overuse in marketing (As someone said it succinctly: HLA. Humans Like Acronyms). I hereby announce my new four part series: AFS (Acronym Fatigue Series), where I will explore my acronym aversion for my readers enjoyment:
This introduction where I explore why I’m wary of acronyms
Part 1: CAP, ACID – Why I’m wary even of formally sound acronyms
Part 2: DRY, KISS – Why I’m wary of well meaning advice acronyms
Part 3: OLAP vs OLTP, ELT vs ETL – Why I’m wary of acronyms pushing technical dichotomies
Acronymic Culture
First and foremost it comes from having a different cultural background. While we do have acronyms at home, they are not as ubiquitous as in English. We use them for institutions and also as abbreviations, but we have very few acronyms. While english has ASAP, BRB, TLDR, AFK, TGIF, LOL, ROFL, and so many more, in Spanish from the top of my head I can only recall TQM (“Te quiero mucho”, I haven’t used this since MSN), NTP (“No te preocupes”, first heard this last year), PQ/XQ (“Por qué/porque”, maybe used to text faster but nowadays I’ve only seen my dad use it).
On the other hand, my introduction to academia was specialized in the humanities, specifically History, but also in other related disciplines, and a bit of philosophy. There, I rarely read acronyms as tools to pack complex concepts and ideas. You don’t see Kant writing TCI instead of “The Categorical Imperative” or Rousseau writing TSC instead of “The Social Contract”. You usually see the creation of concepts (Biopolitics by Foucault, Zeitgeist by Herder, Orientalism by Said) or the use of
nominalization
. This is not to say that these concept packing techniques are not used in Software Engineering. It’s just that acronyms are way less used in the humanities, most probably because of the linguistically diversity in each discipline, while in Computer Science english is the default language for everything.
Note: This is just a thought, less than a thesis, or even a hipothesis. I have no formal proof that acronyms are actually more prevalent in English. Here’s a chart ChatGPT made for me based on
this study’s dataset
(MACRONYM, 2022).
Acronymic Marketing
Having explained why I’m not particularly prone to acronyms by default, I hope the reader can also notice the opposite phenomenon: people (specially native-english speakers) like acronyms. Even in memes,
acronyms spread like fire
.
Note: This is not a criticism of the acronyms themselves (yet). It’s just shedding light into the use of acronyms in marketing to push products.
In part this is because
acronyms are a way of in-group signalling
. On the one hand if you find an unknown acronym in the wild, you are left lost until you find a definition elsewere. But if you understand them, you are left with a sense of feeling as part of the group. This is exploited in tech marketing as a way to signal they are part of the group, and it works! I don’t blame them. In a previous job, marketing spammed so many Cyber intelligence and Cybersecurity acronyms that I doubt any engineering individual contributor in the company was able to define them all. Every new Epic brought its new family of acronyms, some even invented inhouse.
Why am I wary?
Ideas don’t always replicate on their own merit. Ideas specifically abreviated in acronyms are memetic by default, specially well-crafted ones like SOLID (
SOLID
.
isn’t
.
solid
). So when I come across famous acronyms that are spread all over in technical discussions, a part of me always remembers that a tiny reason for that is they are acronyms in the first place.

data.article_summary:
x509-limbo 是一个专门用于评估 X.509 路径验证实现的测试向量套件及配套工具集。该网站为测试套件中的每个测试用例提供友好且可链接的展示界面。

项目设有"trophy case"（荣誉榜），展示通过该套件发现的各类bug实例。x509-limbo 作为 C2SP 项目的组成部分进行维护，最初由 Trail of Bits 创建。

更多详细信息可参阅项目的 GitHub 仓库说明文档。

data.title: Show HN: LLM Thought Visualization
data.author: ninjahawk1
data.article_summary:
Subtext是一个实时可视化工具,用于观察语言模型的内部"思考"过程。它基于Anthropic的研究,使用Jacobian透镜技术将模型在不同层的内部激活状态解码为词汇,从而揭示模型在阅读输入和生成回复时的"心理活动"。

该工具的核心发现包括:模型的判断在输出前就已形成;内部状态显示模型正在"计划"即将说出的词语;可以看到多步推理的中间步骤。系统在9个深度层实时读取模型状态,通过可视化界面展示每个token的内部表征。

技术上基于Qwen3.5-4B模型,使用KV缓存实现流式处理,支持会话导出和浏览器回放。这让研究者能直接观察模型推理的"黑盒"内部过程。
